text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic agree to speed up work on implementing agreement on normalising Yugoslav-Croatian relations.
- Yugoslav parliament to discuss draft law transferring all financial operations to banks.
- Democratic Party of Serbia president says there is strong pressure from within party to join opposition coalition.
- Teachers' strike continues in Belgrade, most schools in interior resume classes.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition coalition partners speed up work on sharing out posts in new Belgrade municipal authorities.
- Health sector to stage warning strike on February 25.
- Civic Alliance of Serbia says over fifty alleged Kosovo Albanian terrorists exposed to police torture in Pristina.
- Germany says Yugoslav authorities blocking payment of German pensions to Yugoslavs.
- Clothing and footwear sector plans strikes, protests, says 450 firms on brink of bankruptcy.
- Serbian authorities, Kosovo Albanians fail to find common ground on university education normalisation.
- Privately-owned TV stations in Serbia form association to fight for their rights.
- Work begins on clearing up 150-tonne oil-spill on Danube, east of Belgrade.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Teachers in Serbia continue protests. Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic says their demands have been politicised.
- Yugoslav and Croatian Foreign Ministers, Milan Milutinovic and Mate Granic, announce signing of 18 bilateral agreements soon.

- Yugoslav and Montenegrin Prime Ministers Radoje Kontic and Milo Djukanovic agree only way out of economic crisis is cooperation with the international community, primarily with financial institutions. Economic activities in the country slowed down by events after local elections in Serbia.
